sampling_model.design: Fixed cohort-stratified repeated cross sections at a common baseline and dates \(1,\ldots,T\), with cohort \(g\) treated from date \(g\) onward.
sampling_model.units: Independent Gaussian cohort-time cell means with known variance \(\sigma^2/(Nq_g)\) at each wave.
sampling_model.treatment: For each \(t\le T-m\), cohort \(g\le t\) is compared with the pooled set \(C_t\); no untreated cohort remains for the target at \(T\).
sampling_model.overlap: Fixed shares satisfy \(c_q/T\le q_g\le C_q/T\), so every control-pool mass used by the score experiment is positive.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: No nuisance function is estimated inside the exact Gaussian score experiment. Calendar smoothness and centered bounded cohort deviations determine affine bias through the explicitly defined leverage functionals \(H(a)\) and \(D(a)\).

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Section 3.3, Proposition 5, shows that sufficiently long-run nonnegative weighted effects are not identified without extrapolation when no never-treated units remain.
The paper identifies group-time ATTs, defines calendar aggregations, and provides simultaneous inference for identified collections.
Proposition 1 derives the repeated-cross-section efficient influence function and its efficiency bound for the two-period ATT.
Gaussian linear-functional difficulty is characterized through a modulus, and affine minimax rules are near global minimax rules.
Known-variance Gaussian confidence procedures over convex regression classes are characterized by ordered moduli and sharp expected-length bounds.
Theorem 3.1 on pp. 15--16 derives a simple honest interval and its Holder boundary bias--variance calibration for nonparametric regression.
Uniformly valid DiD confidence sets are constructed under bounded post-treatment deviations from observed pre-trends.
Loewner covariance dominance and Anderson's theorem order Gaussian procedures for symmetric convex acceptance regions.

body.tldr: Fixed cohort-stratified repeated cross sections induce an exact Gaussian not-yet-treated score experiment with contemporaneous exhaustion and a shared nested-baseline Gram term. The paper exposes the associated baseline-cancellation Pareto program, proves an explicit four-block fast construction and terminal-tail lower certificates, and refutes the proposed unit-normalized interpolation at the exact support boundary. Global minimax MSE and uniformly honest expected length are characterized, with explicit constants, by the exact nested covariance modulus; the Pareto program also supplies a computable affine upper frontier. A closed-form calendar rate remains open, and the matched-date-block calculation applies only to the matched block-diagonal covariance.

project_justification.gap: Staggered-DiD work identifies effects only while valid comparisons remain, whereas Gaussian optimal-recovery work conditions on an already supplied operator and covariance. Neither literature derives the nested score covariance or resolves how cohort-deviation leverage trades against shared-baseline cancellation near the last available score date.
project_justification.niche: The paper treats late-calendar ATT inference as a growing known-covariance Gaussian inverse problem. Its operator-specific content is the exact score covariance, an exposed finite coefficient program, explicit slow and four-block fast geometries, terminal-tail converse inequalities, and a sharp support-boundary refutation.
project_justification.fill: The paper derives the score law, defines the computable baseline-cancellation Pareto frontier, constructs its two endpoint channels, proves lower certificates and the exact boundary behavior, and obtains exact-modulus minimax MSE and honest-length bounds. It does not identify the diagnostic calendar formula with the nested modulus.

body.related_work: Callaway and Sant'Anna provide the group-time causal effects and calendar aggregation underlying the target. Borusyak, Jaravel, and Spiess show why long-run event-study comparisons disappear, motivating extrapolation but not supplying its inference frontier. Sant'Anna and Zhao provide a two-period repeated-cross-section efficiency benchmark. Donoho's Gaussian modulus results and Armstrong and Kolesar's bias-aware interval theory provide generic architecture after an operator and covariance have been supplied; they do not derive the nested staggered-DiD score covariance, the four-block baseline cancellation, or the support-boundary failure of unit-normalized Pareto rates. Rambachan and Roth address untreated-trend sensitivity rather than bounded heterogeneity of the treatment-effect surface. The matched-date-block calculation is a finite-sample calibration for the block-diagonal experiment, not a rate transfer to the nested experiment.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The requested uniform unit-normalized Pareto interpolation is refuted rather than closed positively: its value depends essentially on support slack beyond the ratio encoded by a nominal depth alone. The finite Pareto program, terminal-tail lower bound, localization lower bound, convex-interpolation upper bound, and exact support-boundary values are proved, but a simpler closed form for every interior pair of leverage budgets is not. Equal within-date marginals do not order the nested and matched block-diagonal covariances, and the exact Gaussian analysis does not cover nuisance estimation or non-Gaussian approximation error.
body.honest_scope: The proved headline consists of the exact nested score covariance, the coefficient-energy and bias map, explicit slow and four-block fast arrays, computable Pareto lower and upper bounds, the exact support-boundary refutation, and global MSE and interval-length bounds in terms of the exact nested modulus. The diagnostic calendar functional and its minimizing depth are not asserted to characterize the nested experiment. The matched-date-block Holder rate remains confined to the block-diagonal calibration, while smoothness adaptation remains an open-ended question.
body.interpretation: Pooled one-date weights keep centered cohort-deviation leverage small but retain shared-baseline noise. Signed weights on four ordered reverse-time blocks cancel the baseline loading and achieve the fast energy endpoint at a constant-dilated Holder budget. At the exact boundary budget, however, Holder feasibility forces all date totals onto the first available reverse date, making the small-deviation endpoint infeasible and the budget-one energy of order \(T/m\), not \(T/m^2\). The exact nested modulus and finite Pareto program therefore remain the correct inference objects.
